questions.prompt: Replication lag on a healthy system is bounded to a few milliseconds.
Why can one huge transaction delay everything behind it on a follower?
options: Followers apply changes in commit order

questions.prompt: A leader writes on 32 cores; a follower replays the log on one thread. What happens under heavy write load?
options: The leader slows down to match
The follower falls further and further behind

questions.prompt: What's PostgreSQL's name for log positions? Answer with the acronym. (three letters)
A leader writes 50,000 changes a second, and a follower is 50,000 writes behind. How stale is it?
Why do teams have the leader write a heartbeat row every second?
options: So lag is measured as the age of the newest heartbeat a follower applied, even when the leader is idle

questions.prompt: What should a load balancer do with a follower that's an hour behind?
options: Take it out of the read pool
Keep sending it reads, since it's up
